note: A skipping tune learned in named stages at 40 bpm, then Do, Mi and Sol sung over I and V on a backing track at 40 bpm. The chords are tokens counted the long way, the old Key choice is moves (key any, tempo 40 to 60), the line about another key opens with {{?key}}, and the made-up order carries the one care line.

exercise.title: A skipping tune, then over chords
exercise.why: A skip lands on a chord note, so a tune that skips is really the chord sung one note at a time, and the same notes fit when the chord plays under you.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune at {{=bpm}}: the mic starts with it. Listen once, then press Play again and sing along on the note names.
Sing along with the tune a few times. Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Practice until the skips land without a slide.
{{?key}}In another key the notes change, and the tune still skips up the chord and back.
{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, and {{chord:V}} is the 5th chord, built on {{5}}.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together, at {{=bpm}}. Sing the low {{1}} when {{chord:I}} comes round and {{5}} when {{chord:V}} does. Sing it on "oo".
Then sing {{3}} over {{chord:I}} too, and make up your own order.
_Don't reach for high notes: the low {{1}}, {{3}} and {{5}} are enough._
If you lose the chord, hold {{1}} and wait for {{chord:I}} to come round again.
